qa.question: Can you explain how much of the 9%-11% September quarter growth deceleration versus June is supply constraints versus FX, and what supply constraints beyond advanced SOCs are broadening?
qa.answer: Foreign exchange headwind is around 2.5 percentage points to year-over-year growth rate. Supply constraint impact is expected to increase significantly sequentially from June to September, affecting iPhone, Mac, and iPad. During June, constraints were primarily on Mac, driven by limited flexibility in the supply chain and availability of advanced nodes for SoCs. For September, Tim expects high levels of demand but significantly increased supply constraints with less supply chain flexibility to remedy  it.

qa.question: Does Apple's greater sourcing flexibility for memory aim to ensure supply and mitigate inflation, or primarily to preserve customer value proposition?
qa.answer: Memory costs rose from December to March quarter, expected to rise significantly again in June, and will rise even higher in September. Offsets include carry-in inventory benefits, though benefit will decrease over time, and lower costs on non-memory components. Beyond September, market pricing for memory expected to continue increasing with potential increasing impact on the business. DRAM market has three suppliers; more suppliers could help supply and potentially  pricing.

qa.question: Will you pursue multi-year LTAs with suppliers for supply access at pre-agreed prices, and does pricing strategy protect product gross profit dollars or gross margins?
qa.answer: Prices were raised reluctantly due to 100-year flood of memory pricing with exponential increases. Philosophy looks at units, revenue, and margin together to make business judgment; not a mathematical formula or single dimension. Think about it over long term rather than 90-day clock.

qa.question: Services grew 12% versus guidance, below 10% implied for September. Explain  deceleration drivers and whether App Store headwinds relate to AI reprioritizing user time?
qa.answer: Foreign exchange was main driver of growth rate change from March to June. Other factors: no theatrical F1 release this year versus prior year, and App Store headwinds in mobile gaming. App Store changes in certain countries and court ruling on link-out transactions in US impacted performance. Despite this, App Store set June quarter record. Strong double-digit growth in cloud, video, payment, advertising. Set records in every category.

qa.question: Has demand pull-forward occurred in consumer or enterprise/education markets, and is this factored into forward views?
qa.answer: iPhone has been running 22% growth rate year to date. It's not obvious in the data that pull-forward has occurred. Price increases on iPad and Mac occurred; price elasticity too early to conclude. Channel inventory adjustments take time for consumer response to be understood in weeks ahead.

qa.question: Does AI proliferation at edge open additional addressable market opportunities for Apple beyond current products?
qa.answer: Enormous opportunities for Apple moving forward in AI. Siri AI feedback is excellent. Ability to run percentage of requests on-device is strategic and competitive advantage. Extremely excited about these  opportunities.
